title: The text discusses various environmental issues and initiatives in Southern Africa, focusing on the depletion of fish resources in Namibia, the fight against wildlife poaching in Zambia, and the dangers of using contaminated containers in Kenya. Namibia has banned fishing for a year to protect its fish stocks, while Zimbabwean environmentalists are pushing for environmental impact assessments in development projects. Zambia is taking steps to combat poaching, including forming an Anti-Corruption Commission and a Species Protection Department to investigate illegal hunting. The text also highlights the need for education and community involvement in wildlife protection. In Kenya, there is a warning about the dangers of using recycled containers that may still contain toxic chemicals, emphasizing the need for proper disposal practices.
